question: Which mechanism did India operationalize in 2024 to strengthen regional financial resilience within SAARC?
solution:
The correct answer is __**SAARC Currency Swap Framework (2024-27)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SAARC Currency Swap Framework (2024-27) was operationalized by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to enhance financial cooperation and stability among SAARC member nations.
 
• Under this mechanism, India provides short-term financial assistance in foreign currency to SAARC member countries facing liquidity constraints.
 
• The total corpus for the framework is USD 2 billion, with each eligible member country allowed to withdraw up to USD 400 million within specified limits.
 
• The framework aims to strengthen regional financial resilience, mitigate balance of payment crises, and promote economic stability within the SAARC region.
 
• The currency swap facility is offered in major international currencies (e.g., USD, EUR) or Indian Rupees to support member nations in times of financial distress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SAARC Development Fund (SDF) capital increase**:

 
 
• The SAARC Development Fund was established in 2010 to promote regional integration and economic development in SAARC member states.
 
• It primarily funds projects under its three windows: Social, Economic, and Infrastructure development.
 
• Although increasing the SDF's capital has been proposed, it is not directly linked to the financial resilience mechanisms implemented in 2024.
 
 
 
• **About SAARC**:
 
 
• The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in 1985 to promote economic, social, and cultural cooperation among its eight member states: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.
 
• SAARC initiatives aim to foster regional integration, address common challenges, and promote sustainable development within South Asia.
